title: Measurability of the density positive set
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and for each $x \in \Omega$ let $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) \in  br$ denote the Radon–Nikodym derivative of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$, taken as a real number. Then the set $\left\{x \in \Omega :  rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) \ge 1ight\}$, on which $\mu$ locally dominates $
u$, is a measurable subset of $\Omega$.
hypotheses_covered: μ and ν are probability measures on Ω
replaced: The density positive set $\{x : \mathrm{rnDensity}(\mu,\nu)(x) \ge 1\}$ is a measurable subset of $\Omega$.
